doc.title: Roy McCurdy interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Early drumming influences
summary: Shelly Manne, Kenton west coast groups, then Art Blakey, Max Roach and Kenny Clarke records.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: When you were getting into drums, who were the first people that really grabbed you back then?

When I first, when I first started listening I was listening to probably Shelly Manne. Shelly, guys like that, and then a friend of mine turned me on, well actually we were listening to a lot of west coast music at that time because we were listening to Kenton and we were listening to you know Bob Cooper and all those kind of groups like that, Pete Jolly, all those kind of people. And then a friend of mine came over with an Art Blakey album, “The Jazz Messenger” one of the twelve-inch things you know? It was done at Birdland actually. And I said whoa. And then I started listening to Art. And I was listening to Max back then too I must say, and Joe Jones and people like that, Kenny Clarke. Those were all guys that I was listening to all the time. All those kinds of guys I was listening to constantly. Buying records. Anything they were on I was getting them.
Well I’d like to say that you were on some of the records that made me go “oh, wow!”
